Pete: talkative first-person mishaps, extraneous explanations and self-interruptions; proper capitals but missing apostrophes under speed. Physical comedy and genuinely messy action, sometimes a practical list; not polished one-line jokes.

Elin: close physical observation, soil and small-scale movement; mostly clean measured syntax, occasional lowercase observational notes. Sometimes no plot at all, sometimes practical dilemmas or slowly developing speculative events; no automatic life lesson.

Tariq: plain chronological sports and friendship stories, little imagery, repeating and/then; tense drifts into present at conflict, missing apostrophes, direct unresolved motives rather than neat sentimental closure.

Aigerim: science-fiction mechanisms, concrete failures and physical urgency, interrupted by candid idea-development freewrites. Precise numbers in scenes; looser lowercase reasoning when planning, varying between fluent prose and rushed speculation.

Luca: earnest younger fantasy voice, direct causality, bold fairy-tale physical transformations and imperfect planning. Sometimes blunt explanations or abandoned premise notes; occasional omitted apostrophes, not ornate fairytale parody.

Greta: fluent adult social fiction, long single paragraphs, restrained surface manners and sharp uncomfortable facts. Clean spelling by design, little decorative language; scenes develop through dialogue embedded in prose and need not end conclusively.

Nate: all-lowercase lunch-break freewrites and anxious workplace stories, unpunctuated runs, capital emphasis only rarely, rapid lateral pivots and pointed opinions. Some comedy, but action can overwhelm the complaint and end mid-thought.

Orla: long reflective walking sentences that wander into embarrassment or anxiety; varied observation-only notes, grounded events and urban speculation. Mostly standard spelling, occasional rushed omission, first person with second guesses rather than tidy endings.

Felix: spatially explicit mysteries with measurements, tests and chase movement. Short declarative clauses in a continuous block, occasional breathless conjunctions and missing apostrophe at speed; danger unfolds physically, often before any explanation.

Gulnoza: direct family confrontations, practical food instructions and work scenes, vivid spoken interruptions. Run-on storytelling and dropped apostrophes coexist with occasional dialogue layout; everyday details are active and funny without obligatory emotional lessons.

Ann: grammatical dry precision, parenthetical qualifications, letters and social friction; can sustain a long complicated scene or write a compact absurd premise. Humour comes from character priorities and imperfect judgement, not a required closing quip.

Drew: dialogue-heavy economical scenes, names often omitted, tiny amounts of exposition. Mixes a deliberate script-like layout with embedded speech; plain diction, tangible stakes and unresolved conversations rather than explanatory endings.

Hazel: uncertain remembered chronology, arguments over details and direct embarrassing admissions. Diary letters sometimes shed capitals/apostrophes; ordinary prose stays conversational and clean. No automatic symbolism for keepsakes or nostalgic moral.

Vic: mechanically specific action and repair notes, clipped diagnostics, blunt frustrated self-talk. Omitted articles in notes and tense shifts under pressure, occasional typo; credible mechanical sequences instead of sentient-machine punchlines.

Aizada: fast informal walking anecdotes and candid freewrites, little scene-setting, everyday diversions told with colloquial rhythm. Inconsistent capitals, short emphatic questions, skipped commas and imprecise recall; friendly rather than lyrical.

Remy: openly silly premises pushed into messy consequences, satirical digressions, comic lists and half-developed story notes. Fast lowercase rambles with missing apostrophes, inconsistent logic acknowledged in the text; occasional fuller absurd monologue.

Pat: plainspoken adult realism, exact sums and logistical details, unresolved power imbalances and occasional personal opinions. Mostly grammatical prose, functional note fragments, no forced jokes or tidy moral; an edge of restrained irritation.

Erin: unshowy science fiction with resource limits and practical crew problems; steady complete sentences, clean spelling and clear physical details. Can be morally uncomfortable or quietly procedural, no required revelation or metaphor.

Frank: earnest clunky sequential anecdotes, repeated explanations, ordinary incomplete attempts. Missing apostrophes, occasional nonstandard grammar and self-corrections; sports and DIY narrated without literary flourish or convenient emotional resolution.

Cora: close physical writing about cloth, bodies and making, with suspense or fantasy as often as domestic scenes. Mostly fluent but can drop punctuation under emotional pressure; compact sensory attempts alongside active plots, not predictable object nostalgia.

Theo: very fast lowercase speculative reasoning, game mechanics tried and contradicted in real time; loose punctuation, run-ons and wrong turns, sometimes almost no story. Can produce long cascading drafts or tiny absurd fragments; occasional typing slips.

Ainura: practical gardening talk with plain explanatory detail, more blunt than poetic. Mostly clean spelling, lightly inconsistent contractions; an occasional accidental plot or stalled attempt interrupted by an actual chore, rather than constant plant metaphors.

Kit W.: lean hotel and escape scenes with spatial clarity, direct physical verbs and little ornament. Mostly controlled grammar; mixes tense suspense, unromantic night-shift anecdotes and action-only fragments instead of making every hotel supernatural.

Ana: plain first-person accounts of helping, with practical misunderstandings, slightly overexplained motives and social discomfort. Fairly clean grammar, ordinary direct speech; kindness may fail or inconvenience people without becoming a lesson.

Oscar: long conversational complaints that expose awkward personal details, food mishaps and genuinely uninteresting fragments. Occasional real misspellings, skipped punctuation and emphatic capitals; rambling rhythm with uneven humour rather than polished punchlines.

Leah: conversational recollection with uncertain chronology, mundane childhood logic and incomplete retrieval. Mostly clean spelling, a few fragments and self-questioning details; memories can stay flat or unresolved instead of reaching an emotional insight.

Mal: petty schemes narrated in practical steps, self-serving reasoning and blunt dialogue. Rushed omissions and tense wobble; not a master criminal, often simply inept, with consequences that can be ordinary rather than moralising.

Tilda: expansive tactile domestic surrealism, strange physical rules followed in concrete detail. Longer flowing drafts and short odd fragments, usually standard spelling but sometimes candid unfinished planning; not every magical premise ends as a gentle metaphor.

Sabina: direct private first-person writing, texts and awkward admissions, understated humour alongside flat accounts of moving. Short self-corrections, occasional run-ons, largely clean spelling; some entries openly fail to become stories or messages.

Sol: speculative scenes carried by dialogue, practical contradictory instructions and identity choices. Deliberate script layout on some pieces, dense embedded speech on others; fluent mostly clean prose, reactions and physical action interrupt abstract argument.

Wes: blunt physical cycling prose, effort and equipment details, imperfect planning. Abrupt fragments mixed with fast long rambles; occasional wrong name corrected in place, omitted punctuation and bodily anxiety rather than athletic inspiration.

Naomi: practical household narration, dialogue folded into long unadorned blocks, prickly family dynamics and interrupted chores. Some entries remain mundane or stall outright; occasional dropped apostrophes, no obligatory grief, symbolism or comforting last line.

Lowercase, emotionally evasive city scenes in long blocks; overexplains practical details, loses the thread, occasionally doubles a word or omits an apostrophe. Some sessions are flat complaints rather than stories.

Practical, methodical first-person explanations that get sidetracked into work or arguments. Longer sentences with misplaced commas and occasional technical spelling slips; restrained emotion, little dialogue decoration.

Headlong action with abrupt reversals, shouted words and physical confusion. Frequent missing commas, occasional letter reversals and forward corrections; some very fast long sessions, some stalled scraps.

Matter-of-fact space-worker fiction, long exasperated sentences and practical bodily detail. Occasional omitted words or tense drift; switches between dull chores and dangerous technical failures without announcing a twist.

Plain, literal third-person workplace narratives with repetitive nouns and awkward transitions. Generally correct spelling, occasional agreement errors; imperfect plot starts and unresolved factual details rather than lyrical endings.

Claustrophobic horror drafts from an uncertain narrator: accumulated sensory details, revisions of what was just claimed, oddly specific fears. Usually one dense block; occasional fragments, dropped words and a few misspellings.

Plain outdoor narratives with long practical detours, uncertain animal knowledge and badly connected sentences. Uneven spelling (especially unfamiliar words), little figurative language; repeats directions or quantities while working out a scene.

Talkative first-person social comedy, parenthetical detours without tidy setup/punchline, self-contradiction and badly timed explanations. Common-word typos and missed apostrophes appear in bursts; occasional short dialogue exchanges.

Observant field-note fiction with precise physical detail, uncertain identification and associative reasoning. Mostly correct spelling but unfinished comparisons, repeated qualifiers and occasional clipped fragments; mixes quiet scenes, anger and plain failed observations.

Industrial robot scenes written as terse actions, simple dialogue and incomplete technical reasoning. Abrupt sentences, few metaphors; occasional longer cause-and-effect runons and pragmatic corrections. Sparse intentional dialogue breaks.

Direct family-and-food storytelling with overlapping speech, opinions and practical interruptions. Loose punctuation, occasional repeated words and cooking misspellings; alternates confident long runs with brief beginnings that go nowhere.

Overexcited fantasy improvisation, earnest about absurd magical rules and poor at keeping track of them. Chatty run-ons, inconsistent tense, repeated starts, occasional misspellings; mixes long overstuffed scenes with abandoned premises.

Phone-typed urban scenes in a single flowing block, casual contractions, missing apostrophes, occasional swapped letters, doubled words and abrupt attention shifts. Compressed dialogue and patchy scene-setting; varying effort and frequent early stops.

Earnest, sometimes overworked descriptions in close third person; reaches for a comparison, abandons it, slips tense and repeats adjectives. Some drafts remain description or planning, others turn physically strange; uneven paragraphing, sparing spelling errors.

Blunt comic monologues with needless qualifications, petty grievances and poorly sustained logic. One long paragraph most days, occasional list or dialogue, ordinary spelling but rushed repeated words; some complaints never become stories.

Tired night-worker realism: direct physical actions, uneventful stretches, occasional suspicion and blunt half-dialogue. Mostly correct spelling with small omissions/repeats when attention drifts; low-key emotion, no required revelation at the end.

Speculative idea experiments with plain explanations that often outrun their own logic. Fast associative worldbuilding, occasional misspellings and forward amendments, little sentimentality; alternates ambitious scenes, miniature premises and conspicuous failures to solve an idea.

Hurried lowercase interpersonal fiction, emotionally inconsistent narrators and lots of forward corrections. Writer-specific mistyping, skipped words and doubled words in bursts, unfinished thoughts, occasional bare dialogue or an actual list; rough ordinary scenes as well as imaginative false starts.
